title: Unique Permutations
statement:
List every distinct ordering of numbers that may contain duplicates.

Contract
- `values` is non-null and may contain repeated integers.
- Return each unique permutation of all values exactly once. The empty input has one permutation: the empty list.
- The result order does not matter, but each individual permutation must preserve its chosen order.
- Do not mutate `values`, and make each returned permutation an independent list.

Examples
- `uniquePermutations(new int[]{1, 1, 2})` returns `[[1, 1, 2], [1, 2, 1], [2, 1, 1]]` in any order.
- `uniquePermutations(new int[]{})` returns `[[]]`.
- `uniquePermutations(new int[]{3, 3, 3})` returns `[[3, 3, 3]]`.
hints: Sort a copy so equal values are adjacent.
Skip a duplicate value at one depth when the identical previous value has not been used.
Use a `used` array, copy complete permutations, then undo choices. The probe repeats fixed-size calls, so measured complexity is O(n).
inputSyntax: Input: the values as an array, for example: [1, 1, 2]
